## § 1  What is recognised

¹ The Keeper of the Journal recognises the dignity of Baron of the Bay, held of the Commune of the Bay Area and not of the Republic, and the Barony of the Bay as the estate of the Baron.

² The dignity is a courtesy title, an office of honor, and a standing undertaking.

## § 2  What it is not

¹ It conveys **no jurisdiction**. The Baron judges nothing, and no citizen answers to the Baron.

² It conveys **no precedence**. Every citizen is equal in the Republic and enjoys its equal regard — Article 9 § 1 ¹.

³ It conveys **no exemption**. The Baron is bound by every provision that binds any citizen.

⁴ It is **not hereditary**. Nothing passes by descent, and the Republic belongs to no ancestry — Article 1 § 1 ⁴.

## § 3  What it does convey

¹ The Barony conveys the style of the Baron of the Bay, custody of the Commune's seal, and the duty to affix it to what the Commune has resolved and to nothing else.

## § 4  The undertaking

¹ The dignity is held on the undertaking that the Baron will:

² attend the Commune when it meets, or account in the Journal for their absence;

³ maintain at their own charge whatever the Commune commits to the Barony's keeping; and

⁴ answer any member of the Commune who asks, in the Journal, what has been done in the Barony's name.

⁵ An undertaking not kept for one year is a ground on which the Commune may ask the Court to declare this deed of no effect.

## § 5  Transfer

¹ This deed is transferable — Article 10 § 4 ² applies to it as the deed states.

² The holder undertakes not to transfer it without a resolution of the Commune of the Bay Area.

³ **That undertaking binds the holder and not the deed.** The tools of the Republic will pass this deed on the signed act of whoever holds it, and will not ask the Commune. A transfer made in breach of § 5 ² is effective and is a wrong, and the Commune's remedy is against the transferor in the Court, not against the transferee.

## § 6  Ending

¹ The Baron may renounce the Barony at any time by a signed record, and it then passes to the Commune.

² The Commune may ask the Court to declare this deed of no effect on the ground in § 4 ⁵, or on the ground that the Barony has been used to claim what § 2 withholds.

³ The dignity lapses if the Commune of the Bay Area is dissolved. It is held of the Commune, and cannot outlive it.

## § 7  Validity

¹ This deed is valid because the Keeper has recognised it and it is published in the Journal, and for no other reason — Article 5 § 2 ².
